$comment: Source terms for translating the Nibleaf dashboard, reader and emails. Each locale has glossary/<locale>.json with one entry per id here (translation, plural or short forms, notes), and every catalog string uses those words. doNotTranslate values stay as written in every locale; untranslated.test.ts also accepts a string made only of them, numbers, punctuation and {placeholders}.

terms.definition: One documentation site a team publishes, with its own pages, languages, domain and settings.
terms.note: The main object in the dashboard. Use one word for it everywhere; English uses "site" and "website" interchangeably, translations pick one.

terms.definition: The team account that owns many sites, with members, billing and settings.
terms.note: Never translate as "workspace" (the UI rule is organization, never workspace). English strings that still say workspace mean this.

terms.definition: One document in a site's page tree.
A heading in the page tree that holds pages, without content of its own.
The ordered, nested list of a site's groups and pages in the editor and the reader's sidebar.
Make the current draft the version readers see.
terms.note: Button label: the shortest imperative. A "publish" as a noun is one entry in the publish history.

terms.definition: The unpublished state of a site's pages, which only the team sees.
terms.note: Unpublished changes = changes in the draft.

terms.definition: Edits saved in the draft that readers don't see yet.
Seeing the draft (or the live site) the way readers will.
The published version readers see.
Someone reading a published site. Not a team member.
terms.note: Analytics are about readers; keep it distinct from user and member.

terms.definition: A person with access to an organization or a site.
The page listing an organization's members, invitations and join links.
An email asking someone to join an organization or site.
A shareable link that lets anyone with it join, with a set role.
What a member may do.
The role that can do everything, including deleting the organization.
terms.note: Capitalised as a role name in English; follow the locale's convention for role names consistently.

terms.definition: A site or organization role that manages settings and members.
terms.note: Distinct from a server administrator (operator) in failure messages.

terms.definition: A role that can write and publish pages.
terms.note: Also the name of the editing screen ("the editor"); disambiguate if the locale uses different words.

terms.definition: A role that can read the draft but not change it.
Whoever runs a self-hosted Nibleaf server. Not a site Admin.
A person's own sign-in, profile and preferences.

terms.en: sign in, sign up, sign out
terms.definition: Authentication actions.
terms.note: Use the locale's standard UI verbs; one pair everywhere.

terms.definition: Configuration screens.
The first settings section (name, address, basics).
The settings section for theme, colours, logo and layout of the reader.
A set of colours and styles for the reader; also light/dark mode.
A site's own address (docs.example.com) instead of the Nibleaf address.
Where a site is reachable.
A rule sending an old URL to a new one.
Who can read a published site: public, password, or signed-in members.
An optional site feature turned on in Settings (search, Ask AI, preview deployments…).
A connection to another service (Git, Discord, webhooks).
A URL Nibleaf calls on events.
terms.note: Many locales keep the English loanword; follow the locale's common developer usage.

terms.definition: A secret for calling the Nibleaf API.
A secret credential (access token).
A parallel version of a site's content (Git sense).
Keeping content in step with a Git repository.
Bringing existing docs in (from Mintlify, GitBook, Markdown…).
Downloading a site's content.
A content language a site is published in (and the dashboard's interface language).
terms.note: Source language = the one translations start from.

terms.definition: The reader feature that answers questions from the site's pages.
terms.note: Feature name: translate as a short imperative phrase readers understand, and use it identically everywhere.

terms.definition: The dashboard page that writes and edits with AI.
Per-site AI settings (model, budget).
The section with reader statistics.
How many times pages were loaded.
Reading sessions.
Reader searches on the site.
Readers' "Was this helpful?" answers and comments.
The time window of a report (last 7 days, custom range).
Showing change against the window before.

terms.en: Web Vitals (Main content shows up, Responds to clicks, Layout stays still)
terms.definition: Page-speed measurements; the card names are plain-language, the abbreviations (LCP, INP, CLS) stay in English.
Bots of AI services reading the site, and how the site appears in AI answers.
The subscription tier.
How much of a plan's limits is used.
Payment settings.
In-app and email alerts.
Earlier saved versions of a page or site, and bringing one back.
Making an earlier publish live again.
Problems found before publishing (broken links, missing titles).
terms.note: "Fix" button on each check: short imperative.

terms.definition: The settings section with irreversible actions (delete, transfer).
Delete = destroy permanently; remove = take out of a list (a member, a domain).
Form saving.
Dismiss without changes.
Clipboard actions.
Running Nibleaf on your own server (vs Nibleaf Cloud).
The signed-in app where teams manage sites.
The screen where pages are written.
A content element inserted in a page (callout, tabs, steps, card).
A highlighted note block (Note, Tip, Warning).
